dedupe_keys.name: meta high resolution population density maps and demographic estimates hrsl

description: These maps estimate the number of people living in 30-metre grid tiles, with demographic layers such as children under five and people aged 60 and over. Meta used machine learning to identify buildings in commercially available satellite imagery and, with partners at Columbia University, overlaid population estimates from public census data and other statistics; the maps are not built from Facebook user data. They are published by AI for Good at Meta on the Humanitarian Data Exchange as country datasets of downloadable GeoTIFF tiles, under CC BY, with the recommended citation to the Facebook Connectivity Lab and CIESIN High Resolution Settlement Layer (2016, source imagery by DigitalGlobe). The cross-cutting harvest queued the United States, Indonesia, Peru, the Philippines, the United Arab Emirates, Ireland and Eswatini datasets. Caveats: Meta states that since 2024 the maps are no longer being updated, estimates depend on building detection in imagery and on census inputs. They provide fine-scale population exposure for hazard exposure, emergency response and service capacity planning, including for infrastructure outages; related records are the WorldPop and GRID3 census gridded population estimates and the Copernicus Global Human Settlement Layer.
